questions.prompt: A prospect's company just announced a new CFO after the previous one left abruptly. According to the lesson, why is this a useful trigger for outreach?
choices: It means the company is in financial distress and needs help immediately.
New finance leadership typically re-evaluates existing vendors and wants to put their stamp on the tech stack.
CFOs are always the economic buyer for software purchases.
It gives you a reason to congratulate them, which builds rapport.
questions.explanation: Leadership changes — especially at the CFO, CRO, or CMO level — create a natural window because incoming executives often review and re-evaluate vendor relationships in their first 90 days.

questions.prompt: You are about to paste prospect information into an AI tool to build a pre-call brief. Which of the following inputs is safe to use with a public AI model?
choices: Deal notes your AE wrote after a confidential discovery call
The prospect's contact email address from your CRM
A press release the company published last week about a new product launch
Your company's internal pricing sheet for this account
questions.explanation: Public information — press releases, LinkedIn profiles, news articles — is safe to use with general-purpose AI tools. CRM notes, contact data, and internal pricing contain private company or customer data that should only be processed in approved internal tools.

questions.prompt: A rep wants to use AI to score an account against their ICP. They have collected a LinkedIn company page summary and a recent TechCrunch funding announcement. Which prompt approach best follows the lesson guidance?
choices: Ask AI to search the web for more information about the company before scoring it.
Paste the public data and ask AI to score the account against a described ICP, flagging fit reasons and trigger events.
Ask AI to generate a complete outreach sequence based on the funding news alone.
Ask AI to predict the company's revenue so you can qualify budget before reaching out.
questions.explanation: The ICP scorecard prompt works by feeding AI the public data you have collected and asking it to evaluate fit against your defined ICP criteria — combining your research with AI's ability to process and synthesize information quickly.
